questions.q: Which table stores the records that define how ServiceNow handles a reply to a notification email?
options: sysevent_email_action
sysevent_email_template
sysevent_in_email_action
sys_watermark
questions.explain: sysevent_in_email_action governs inbound email processing — the direction opposite outbound notifications.

questions.q: How does ServiceNow actually determine which record a reply email belongs to?
options: It always creates a brand-new record for every inbound email, regardless of content
It parses the visible subject line text alone and guesses based on keywords
It scans for a watermark — a hidden reference echoed back in the reply — that uniquely identifies the originating record
An administrator must manually link every inbound email to a record
questions.explain: The watermark, typically embedded in the outbound notification and quoted back in the reply, is what lets inbound processing match definitively rather than guessing from a subject line.

questions.q: A reply to an incident notification is correctly matched by its watermark. What does a typical Inbound Email Action do with that reply?
options: Deletes the original Incident record
Sends a new outbound notification back to the same caller automatically
Runs a script against the matched Incident, commonly appending the reply's text as a work note or comment
Converts the Incident into a Catalog Task
questions.explain: A Record Action's script runs against the matched record, with the reply's subject, body, and sender available — appending it as a work note is a common real example.

questions.q: What distinguishes a Reply from a New inbound email in ServiceNow's processing?
options: A Reply always comes from an admin account, while New always comes from an end user
A Reply is matched to an existing record via a watermark; a New inbound email has no watermark match and can instead create a brand-new record
There is no distinction; all inbound email is handled identically
A Reply can only be processed if it contains an attachment
questions.explain: Reply, Forward, and New are the three situations inbound processing distinguishes between, based on whether a watermark match occurred and how.

questions.q: Why does getting an Inbound Email Action's script right (clean appending, no duplicated quoted text) matter for end users?
options: It has no real effect on the end-user experience
It determines whether the caller's email client crashes
It keeps the reply-to-update experience trustworthy, instead of producing messy or duplicated work notes that make the record harder to read
It controls whether the notification's trigger condition fires at all
questions.explain: The watermark-and-matching machinery is invisible to the end user; a poorly written inbound action script is what actually surfaces as a confusing, messy record.
